hero.title: Portofino
hero.subtitle: Italian cooking, the open sea, and a terrace that runs straight onto the sand.

story.title: A table at the water's edge
body: Portofino began as a small kitchen behind the Old Souk, cooking for the fishermen who tied up a few metres from the door. The recipes came from Liguria; the fish came from Jounieh Bay. Very little has changed since.
We still buy the catch at the port in the morning, still roll the pasta by hand, and still set the tables so close to the water that the first row hears it.

terrace.title: Dinner with your feet almost in the sea
body: Thirty tables under white parasols, a run of steps down to the sand, and the whole bay in front of you. Lunch is bright and unhurried; by nine the lanterns are lit and the water has gone dark.
The front row books out first — tell us if you want it and we will do our best.

music.title: Live music every Friday and Saturday
music.body: A trio on the terrace from nine, and through the summer a rotating cast of performers — a singer one week, a quartet the next. No cover charge, no minimum. Just book early, because the terrace fills.

aside.title: Good to know
items: Tables on the front row of the terrace are limited — ask and we will do our best.
Weekend evenings book out several days ahead, especially when there is live music.
For groups of nine or more, or a private event, please call us directly.
We hold your table for fifteen minutes. Running late? A quick call keeps it.
